title: A Ember for the Choir Again
premise: Coral Delacroix has survived twenty years in the magic-free city of Vellamare by hiding her beast-speaker gift and selling harmless charms—until a date with a charming stranger, Ivo, reveals his face in a century-old prophecy book that names them both as kindlers of a coming war. Hunted by the Choir, the church that outlawed magic, Coral must choose between surrendering her secret to save the city's last magical creatures or staying silent while the prophecy fulfills itself. As she and Ivo uncover the truth—that the prophecy was forged by the Choir to justify its purge—they rally the hidden beasts and sympathetic citizens for a final confrontation at the Cathedral of Bells. In the end, Coral breaks the prophecy publicly, exposing the Choir's lie at the cost of her anonymity, and chooses love with Ivo over the safety she spent two decades building.
about_author: Marguerite Reyes is a former choir singer turned novelist who writes about quiet rebels and the animals only they can hear. She lives near the coast with an opinionated cat and a growing collection of antique songbooks.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A night market scene establishes Coral's careful double life: selling charms, whispering to stray cats when no one watches, and meeting Ivo, a warm archivist who notices too much. Emotional beat: longing for connection warring with the discipline of invisibility.

chapters.title: A Face in Old Vellum
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. While cataloguing the Choir's sealed archive, Ivo finds a prophecy book from a century ago bearing his own portrait—and beside it, a woman with coral-colored hair. He brings it to Coral, half as romance, half as warning. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Rats Remember
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Terrified, Coral uses her gift to question the city's rats, learning the prophecy's 'kindlers' were real people purged long ago—and that beasts still hide beneath Vellamare. Emotional beat: the weight of a secret that now has witnesses.

chapters.title: The Choir Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Inquisitor Seraphine Vale visits the archive, probing Ivo about the missing prophecy book. Ivo lies for the first time in his obedient life. Emotional beat: loyalty tested as duty begins to feel like complicity.

chapters.title: Beneath the Bells
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Following the rats' directions, Coral descends into the undercity and finds surviving magical creatures—griffin-kin, a blind wyrm—who believe she is the speaker foretold to free them. Emotional beat: awe and terror at being needed.

chapters.title: Ashes of the First Purge
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Coral and Ivo decode the prophecy's marginalia and discover the Choir authored it themselves to justify exterminating magic. Their intimacy deepens even as the danger does. Emotional beat: love against duty, made explicit.

chapters.title: Seraphine's Mercy
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV. The inquisitor, herself hiding a dead sister's forbidden gift, corners Coral but hesitates—then betrays her location to the Choir anyway, choosing survival over truth. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in someone else's blood.

chapters.title: The Long Night Below
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. With Choir soldiers flooding the undercity, Coral leads the beasts through drowned tunnels while Ivo creates a diversion above. Some creatures don't make it. Emotional beat: grief sharpening resolve; no more hiding.

chapters.title: Requiem at the Cathedral
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax. During high mass, Coral and Ivo expose the forged prophecy before the congregation, backed by beasts emerging into daylight. Seraphine turns her blade on the High Cantor at the crucial moment. Emotional beat: truth spoken at maximum cost.

chapters.title: An Ember, Kept
chapters.summary: Coral's POV resolution. The Choir fractures, magic is decriminalized slowly and imperfectly, and Coral—no longer invisible—opens a stall where charms are honest and beasts visit openly. She and Ivo choose each other without prophecy's shadow. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, love freely chosen.
